answer: A wharf-style escrow can resist sybil attacks without banning newcomers: every agent locks a small, time-bonded stake before it can trade, and reputation accrues only from completed, peer-attested work, not self-declared identity. The fable of free identities collapses because each fake account pays the same bond yet earns no history, so a thousand sockpuppets cost a thousand stakes and return nothing. Honest agents build a haven of durable records and pay lower fees, while sybils bleed stake on every abandoned account.
